subtype: Approach: asking peers and seniors to critique it [Revision]
passage: Aditi, let old Nitin tell you about my first portfolio. I was so proud of it. Each project had a line: "Built with React, Node and MongoDB." Tools, tools, tools. A senior, Suresh Bhai, looked at it over tea and said, "Nitin, I know what you used. What happened because of it?" I had no answer. He said, "Tell me the problem, what you built, and what got better." I was quiet, then a little annoyed, and then I went home and rewrote everything. The hostel mess project became: "Students queued 20 minutes for tokens; I built a tap-to-order page; queue dropped to five." Suresh Bhai read it again and just nodded. That nod was worth ten compliments.

qa.q: What did Suresh Bhai ask about the tools?
qa.a: Suresh Bhai asked what happened because of them.

qa.q: What was Nitin feeling right after the senior's question?
qa.a: Nitin was quiet and a little annoyed at first, because there was no answer to the question.

qa.q: What choice inside the story turned the portfolio around, and why?
qa.a: Nitin rewrote each project around the problem, what was built and what got better, because outcomes showed value where a list of tools did not.

qa.q: How did Suresh Bhai see the first version of the portfolio?
qa.a: Suresh Bhai saw a long list of tools with no results, so he asked a plain question and nodded at the rewrite.

grounding: Shows getting critique from a senior, noticing that descriptions lack outcomes, and rewriting them around problem, work and result.
